item.title: When women organise, democracy survives: Why gender justice cannot be a casualty of global crises
item.description: “Across regions, feminist movements and women-led civil society organisations face a convergence of crises that threatens decades of hard-won progress ... ”

item.title: Democracy needs women: Feminist leadership in times of shrinking enabling environments for civil society
item.description: When feminist leadership expands, democracy deepens. It becomes more accountable, inclusive, and participatory. Women’s civic participation is not about political correctness but about democratic survival.

item.title: Government attacks on mainstream media undermine the credibility of democracy in Botswana
item.description: "What is at stake in Botswana media is not only law reforms but the viability of journalism in a disrupted, underfunded and rapidly changing environment."

item.title: Rumeen Farhana on politics, purpose, and the fight ahead in Bangladesh
item.description: From BNP stalwart to expelled independent, Rumeen Farhana rode the ‘duck’ symbol to a 38,000-vote victory in Brahmanbaria-2, defying harassment, party betrayal, and Bangladesh’s bruising gendered political battlefield.

item.title: Ethiopia’s urban renewal projects and turn toward aesthetic propaganda
item.description: This is not a trend limited to Ethiopia. Influencers have increasingly become important in popularizing selective authoritarian stories from Dubai to China, and thereby legitimizing authoritarian narratives.

item.title: The normalization of Uyghur repression in the name of ’social governance’ in China
item.description: Chinese official discourse has increasingly used “social governance” to describe policies in the Uyghur region. This neutral administrative language is reshaping people's perception of repression, assimilation, and social control.

item.title: From Gaza to Lebanon and Iran: The normalization of atrocity
item.description: The destruction of Gaza did not remain confined there. Predictably, it has become a precedent, shaping the wars in Lebanon and Iran as international law erodes under selective outrage.

item.title: From menstrual dignity to digital safety: How grassroots feminists are redefining gender justice
item.description: What connects a pad box in a Nigerian school, a coalition meeting in Pakistan, and a digital security workshop in Paraguay? They each address a structural barrier that limits women’s participation.

item.title: LGBTQ+ rights worsen in several countries following US policy changes
item.description: “Within LGBTQIA+ spaces, gay men are visible. For women, there is no space. Gay men should use their privilege to create space for queer women.’

item.title: Forbidden movies: Russia bans films that reject so-called ‘traditional values’
item.description: 'Traditional values' in the law include patriotism, service to the fatherland, high morals, a strong family, productive labor, and the priority of the spiritual over the material.
